title: Inventory Control at Cosic: An Industry Study
subtitle: Process mapping, key performance measurement analysis, and strategy recommendations.
html:
View full presentation · Canva ↗

Connecting inventory metrics to warehouse work

This project examines inventory control at COSIC across capacity, turnover, location accuracy, equipment availability, and invoicing. It asks why recorded stock can still be difficult to locate and process, with consequences for putaway, dispatch, and cash collection.

Locating bottlenecks through process mapping

The process map follows arrival, WMS scanning, slot checks, putaway, paper location logs, manual invoicing, and customer payment. It identifies an information gap between paper location records and subsequent data entry, as well as extra handling when storage slots are occupied.

The presentation reports approximately two inventory turns, a 48-hour invoicing delay, and 90% location accuracy. Comparing record accuracy, location accuracy, inventory days, and dock-to-stock time shows why a correct stock count does not necessarily mean goods can be found and processed efficiently.

Proposals for visibility and equipment availability

The first recommendation combines RFID tags, fixed dock readers, and handheld devices to improve location visibility and reduce searching and counting effort. The accuracy and productivity figures presented are proposed benefits, not completed results.

The second establishes a forklift battery swap-and-charge schedule with a spare battery to reduce equipment waiting time. Together, the proposals address information and physical-resource constraints rather than treating warehouse performance as a single inventory problem.

Why the project matters

Inventory performance depends on where goods are stored, how quickly they can be processed, and whether information flows into invoicing and payment. The project translates performance gaps into specific operational and equipment choices.

Current-state figures come from the presentation; RFID and equipment scheduling are recommendations.
